newsitem.title: INDIA: India tea prices firm on demand, low world supply.
newsitem.headline: India tea prices firm on demand, low world supply.

text.p: Indian tea prices have firmed on strong demand from overseas and low global supplies, traders said on Tuesday.
They said domestic tea prices had risen by about 5,000 rupees per tonne since the beginning of the season in January 1997.
"There is strong buying from Russia, Poland, Germany and West Asia," Thatha Rangaiah, chairman of the Coonoor Tea Trade Association, told Reuters.
Traders said a sharp dip in tea output in Sri Lanka and Kenya had badly affected global supplies.
Kenya produced 54.97 million kg of tea between January and April 1997, a fall of about 38.47 million kg compared with the same period in 1996.
Sri Lanka's output fell by about 2.2 million kg to 38 million between January and March 1997. Indonesia's output fell by 3.3 million in the same period, industry officials said.
"Therefore, many countries are looking towards India," Veeraghavan Ramaswamy, director, Carrit Moran and Company, told Reuters.

Rangaiah said India sold 26 million kg of tea between January and May 1997, compared with 17 million in the same period last year. "We got an average price of about 47.09 rupees per kg this year against 41.90 rupees last year."

Traders said India's tea output in calendar 1997 was expected to be about 760 million kg, down from 780 million last year. "Still the demand for Indian tea would be higher because of an expected global shortage."
India produced 52.52 million kg of tea between January and March 1997, down from 58.78 million in the same period last year.
Traders and industry officials said adverse weather in the main growing areas in the northeastern states had affected harvest operations.
Industry officials said India needed to increase its productivity to meet rising international demand and retain its world markets.
"Otherwise, India has to be content as a substitute market," said Subodh Paul, general manager of Contemporary Tea Services, a leading auctioneer.
